system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: Its built-in TypeScript harness gives any model the context and environment it needs for truly autonomous work: sessions, tools, skills, instructions, filesystem access, and a secure sandbox to run in.
system_prompt_style.note: System prompt assembled from agent function return plus useSkill/useTool composition; no prompt file opened.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: a secure environment where they can use tools, modify files, and autonomously complete real work

context_compaction.note: A compaction-test example file exists (examples/hello-world/src/agents/compaction-test.ts) but no mechanism evidence available.

observation_format.note: Images appear supported (with-image example) but no conversion code in evidence; raw_text inferred from tool/text harness.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: **[Tools](https://flueframework.com/docs/guide/tools/)** — Give agents typed actions for calling APIs, querying data, and making controlled changes through your application.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: **[MCP Servers](https://flueframework.com/docs/guide/tools/#connect-mcp-tools)** — Connect agents to authenticated tools and services through the open Model Context Protocol ecosystem.
tool_schema_source.note: Tools are typed TypeScript functions registered via useTool, so schemas derive from types.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: Connect agents to authenticated tools and services through the open Model Context Protocol ecosystem.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: Build agents that can keep context across conversations and events as they autonomously work toward a goal.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: You give them a task — not a pre-defined series of steps — and trust them to complete it using the context and tools that you provide.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: **[Subagents](https://flueframework.com/docs/guide/subagents/)** — Define specialized roles for different tasks, then let your agent delegate work to the right expert.
multi_agent_topology.note: Default agent composes no subagents; orchestrator_workers reachable via subagents feature.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: then let your agent delegate work to the right expert
delegation_mechanism.note: Opt-in subagent_spawn reachable via the Subagents feature; default example agent declares none.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: Build agents that can keep context across conversations and events as they autonomously work toward a goal.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: **[Skills](https://flueframework.com/docs/guide/skills/)** — Package reusable expertise and workflows that agents can load whenever a task needs specialized guidance.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: **[Durability](https://flueframework.com/docs/guide/durability/)** — Learn how agents preserve progress through failures and restarts with durable recovery for accepted work.

self_verification.note: Docs list vitest-evals tooling but no harness-enforced verification evidence.

execution_isolation.note: Example uses local() sandbox from @flue/runtime/node; container/remote sandboxes (Daytona, E2B, Modal, Cloudflare) shipped as ecosystem options.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: sessions, tools, skills, instructions, filesystem access, and a secure sandbox to run in

tracing.evidence_quote: Monitor your agents and export telemetry with [OpenTelemetry](https://flueframework.com/docs/ecosystem/tooling/opentelemetry/), [Braintrust](https://flueframework.com/docs/ecosystem/tooling/braintrust/), [Sentry](https://flueframework.com/docs/ecosystem/tooling/sentry/), or your own observer.
tracing.note: Adapter package @flue/opentelemetry must be installed; not on by default.

eval_hooks.note: Evals guide and vitest-evals tooling blueprint ship in repo; not a benchmark runner per se.

target_domain.evidence_quote:
Triage a bug report end-to-end: reproduce the bug,
diagnose the root cause, verify whether the behavior is
intentional, and attempt a fix.

open_source.note: LICENSE file present at repo root; licence text not in evidence.

model_agnostic.note: Provider-prefixed model ids plus a provider-api reference doc indicate multi-provider support.

first_release_date.note: A blog post 'flue-1-0-beta' exists but no release date in evidence.
